plan.visual_reading: The arc opens on the crowd's scorn (the shaking heads), lifts to the psalmist who foresaw it, descends through the curled lip / wagging passers-by / sneering rulers into the enduring Christ, turns on 'He could have come down' (held power) and the scorn borne in love, and lands on the mocked King who stayed — the cross at dawn, an open invitation. Hero #7 (the cross) bookends so it lands on Christ.
plan.red_team_notes: Jaded Viewer risks: many jeering-face scenes (1,3,5,9) could blur into one angry crowd — varied framings (close/mid/low-angle/wide) and the turn to mercy (13) offset it. The 'script/psalm' beat is the writing trap — solved by a VISION (2), no scroll/text. Back half is crucifixion-heavy (6,7,10,11,12,14) but that is the passage; framings vary and the mocker scenes anchor the front half.

scenes.title: The Shaking Heads
scenes.rationale: Jeering faces at the cross's foot — the arresting scorn.
scenes.visible_elements: jeering first-century faces shaking their heads at the foot of a cross, lips curled.
scenes.subject_block: a tight cluster of jeering first-century Judean faces at the foot of a rough wooden upright, the heads tilted and shaken mid-scorn, lips curled and shot out in derision, eyes narrowed upward in contempt, weathered ancient skin and coarse dust-toned robes, the whole sunk in a brown-black ground with hard low light on the nearest sneer

scenes.title: A Script, A Thousand Years Old
scenes.purpose: Point: the mockery was foretold in Psalm 22.
scenes.rationale: Show the psalmist SEEING it, not a scroll (no garbled text).
scenes.visible_elements: an aged psalmist gazing toward a dim distant mocked figure on a far rise; no text.
scenes.subject_block: an aged first-century Hebrew psalmist seen from the side in a coarse mantle, his lined face lifted and his eyes wide toward a dim far-off rise where a single bound figure stands surrounded by tiny shadowed mockers, his weathered hand pressed to his breast, the foreground rocks dark, the distance hazed in dust and prophetic light, no writing or scroll present anywhere
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of foresight reaching across centuries

scenes.title: They Shoot Out The Lip
scenes.purpose: Proof (Ps 22:7): the curled lip of scorn.
scenes.rationale: A single mocking face, restrained not cartoonish.
scenes.visible_elements: a single mocking first-century face filling the view, lower lip thrust out and curled.
scenes.subject_block: a single mocking first-century Judean face filling the view, the lower lip thrust out and curled in derision, teeth just bared, the eyes lifted in cold scorn, weathered sun-worn skin in hard raking light, the rest of the head sunk in deep shadow
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a face set in scorn

scenes.title: The Passers-By Wag Their Heads
scenes.rationale: The crowd at the cross + the echoing vignettes.
scenes.visible_elements: a knot of passers-by at the cross wagging their heads; the dim crucified Christ above; vignettes.
scenes.subject_block: a wide view at the foot of a tall wooden cross, a knot of passers-by with heads wagged in scorn and dust-toned robes, the crucified Christ robed at the waist dim and small above them against a darkening sky, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting more wagging heads, a jabbing finger, a turned scornful back, and an aged psalmist's hand half-dissolved in the dark
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a passing crowd's contempt

scenes.title: The Rulers Sneer
scenes.rationale: The rich-robed rulers in smug contempt.
scenes.visible_elements: robed rulers in rich layered robes, faces lifted in smug contempt, a finger jabbed up.
scenes.subject_block: two robed first-century religious rulers in rich layered robes and prayer fringes seen close, their faces lifted in smug contempt toward an unseen cross above, one with a finger extended upward in accusation, the other's lip curled, dim onlookers half-dissolved behind them, warm low light on the smug brow against deep shadow

scenes.title: He Trusted In God
scenes.purpose: Proof: the crucified Christ enduring the recorded taunt.
scenes.rationale: Christ on the cross, bowed, enduring, reverent.
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ enduring on the cross, head bowed, against a dark sky.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ on a rough wooden cross seen at mid distance against a darkened noon sky, the thorn-crowned head bowed low in endurance, the body robed at the waist, the arms taut along the beam, a faint sorrowful stillness on the face, the small dim forms of jeering figures at the foot

scenes.title: The King Who Would Not Come Down
scenes.purpose: THE HERO — the gospel-pivot: the King who stayed on the cross.
scenes.rationale: Iconic reverent crucifixion; bookends the cut.
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ on the cross, head bowed in sovereign stillness, faint light behind.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ lifted on a rough wooden cross seen from a low reverent angle against a darkening sky, the thorn-crowned head bowed in sovereign stillness, the body robed at the waist, the arms taut along the beam, a faint pale light breaking behind the dark hill, the small forms of mockers dim and turned away at the foot, the very top of the cross bare and plain with no inscription board and no lettering
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a King who stays, sovereign and still

scenes.title: Unwilling Witnesses
scenes.purpose: Proof: the scorners unknowingly reciting the prophecy.
scenes.rationale: Mockers foreground dark, the luminous Christ beyond.
scenes.visible_elements: the dark backs of jeering mockers in front; the luminous crucified Christ beyond; vignettes.
scenes.subject_block: the dark backs and raised arms of a jeering crowd filling the foreground, and beyond them the crucified Christ small and luminous on the cross under a pale dusk sky, the mockers unknowingly framing him, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting an open scornful mouth, a raised fist, a far rough cross, and an aged psalmist's lifted hand half-dissolved in the dark
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of enemies who testify without knowing

scenes.title: If Thou Be The Son Of God
scenes.purpose: Conviction: the 'come down' taunt hurled up.
scenes.rationale: A mocker jeering up at the cross; Christ silent above.
scenes.visible_elements: a mocker's open-mouthed jeer hurled upward, the cross looming above.
scenes.subject_block: a single first-century mocker seen from a low angle, the head thrown back and the mouth open mid-jeer toward a rough cross looming dark above against a bruised sky, one arm flung upward in derision, the dim crucified figure small and still at the top of the beam, hard light on the jeering throat and jaw against deep shadow
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a taunt flung at the silent cross

scenes.title: He Could Have Come Down
scenes.purpose: Conviction: restrained power — He chose to stay.
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ central and dominant; dim restrained power vignettes around.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ at the centre and clearly dominant on the cross, calm and unbroken against a dark sky, and faint and barely-there in the surrounding shadow the power he holds back, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting dim ranks of restrained angelic figures, a held and unfallen bolt of light, the unbroken iron nails, and a steady unshaken face
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of sovereign power willingly restrained
vignettes: dim ranks of restrained angelic figures
a held unfallen bolt of light

scenes.title: Bearing The Scorn
scenes.purpose: Conviction: Christ bears the scorn with willing love.
scenes.rationale: Christ's face close, enduring with love not pain.
scenes.visible_elements: a close reverent view of the crucified Christ's face, eyes lowered in willing endurance.
scenes.subject_block: a close reverent view of the crucified Christ's face inclined and the eyes lowered in willing endurance rather than pain, a thorn-marked brow, the jaw set in quiet resolve, warm light catching one cheek against deep shadow, the grain of the dark beam just behind
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of scorn borne in willing love

scenes.title: The King They Told To Come Down
scenes.rationale: The crucified Christ as King, a faint regal light, still on the cross.
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ on the cross with a faint regal stillness, the scorn quieting around.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ on the cross seen at mid distance, the thorn-crowned head lifted slightly in a faint regal stillness, the body robed at the waist, a warm break of light beginning behind the dark hill, the jeering figures at the foot now small and falling into shadow, the cross reading like a throne
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a mocked King revealed as King

scenes.title: For The Very People Throwing It
scenes.purpose: Landing: He bore it FOR the mockers.
scenes.rationale: Christ above looking down on the upturned faces; vignettes of a softening.
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ above looking down on upturned scornful faces; a softening; dawn.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ on the cross above looking down with mercy on a field of upturned first-century faces below, some still scornful and one beginning to soften and lower its eyes, warm dawn light beginning across the quiet ground, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting a clenched fist loosening, a bowed shamed head, an open empty hand, and a far gathered company in dawn light
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of mercy poured on the mockers
vignettes: a far gathered company in dawn light

scenes.title: Come To The One Who Would Not Come Down
scenes.purpose: Landing CTA: the cross at dawn, the King who stayed.
scenes.rationale: The cross against a widening dawn — the invitation.
scenes.visible_elements: the cross against a widening gold dawn, the still King upon it, an open invitation.
scenes.subject_block: the rough cross standing against a widening gold dawn, the thorn-crowned Christ still and reverent upon it, warm light breaking from behind the upright beam across a quiet land, the hill's crest in soft shadow, the jeering crowd gone, the scene hushed and open in dawn light
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of an open invitation to the King who stayed

plan.rationale: Hero = the cross (7): the mocked King who would not come down is the gospel-pivot. Kept 4 unified scenes (4,8,10,13) carrying the NT-link and the two OT echoes (the psalmist #2, the unwilling-witnesses #8 reciting Ps 22). Rejected any scroll/written-script scene (Kling garbles letters) for a vision (#2). Front-loaded the mocker faces; the back half is the enduring/merciful King.

panel.note: Arc carries the turn: scorn (#1) -> the foretelling psalmist (#2) -> the curled lip / wagging crowd / sneering rulers proof -> 'He could have come down' (#10) -> the mocked King who stayed (#7,#12,#14). Not a slideshow of angry faces.

No invented narrative — the psalmist (#2) is shown SEEING, not writing; the mockers are exactly Matthew's record; 'He could have come down' (#10) keeps Sonship a CHOICE, not the mockers' 'cannot save' taunt. No unwarranted halos.

14 scenes in window; state-only subject_blocks; 3-5 macro anchors each; each earns its slot.

paper_cohesion.notes: The set coheres as one study. The thread (the mockers reciting Psalm 22; the King who would not come down) is unbroken: the scorn opens (#1), the psalmist foresaw it (#2), the proof descends through the lip/wagging-heads/rulers (#3,#4,#5) onto the enduring Christ (#6), the scorners testify unknowingly (#8), and the turn lands on held power (#10), borne scorn (#11), and the mocked King revealed (#12) who bore it FOR the mockers (#13), closing on the cross at dawn (#14). Hero #7 (the cross) bookends so it lands on Christ. No invented eyewitness, no written-scroll scene. The only soft spot is a front-half mocker-face cluster, intrinsic to the passage and offset by framing variety and the mercy turn — not a structural failure.
